feed.title: Science & Academia — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Agriculture
entry.summary: A list of open-source technology and tools for farming and gardening.

entry.title: Awesome Bioinformatics
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for analysing biological data (bioinformatics).

entry.title: Awesome Citizen Science
entry.summary: A list for community-based, non-institutional science (citizen science).

entry.title: Awesome Clean Tech
entry.summary: A list of projects and resources fighting climate change with technology.

entry.title: Awesome Computational Biology
entry.summary: A list of resources for computational approaches to biology problems.

entry.title: Awesome Healthcare
entry.summary: A list of open-source healthcare software for facilities.

entry.title: Awesome Information Retrieval
entry.summary: A list of information-retrieval resources for learning to build your own search engine.

entry.title: Awesome LaTeX
entry.summary: A list of packages, templates and tools for LaTeX, the scientific typesetting language.

entry.title: Awesome Neuroimaging
entry.summary: A list of imaging software for analysing brain data from living subjects.

entry.title: Awesome Neuroscience
entry.summary: A list of computational resources for studying the nervous system and brain.

entry.title: Awesome Quarto
entry.summary: A resource list for Quarto, the scientific and technical open-source publishing system.

entry.title: Awesome Scientific Computing
entry.summary: A list of tools and libraries for solving complex scientific problems by computer.

entry.title: Awesome Theoretical CS
entry.summary: A list for the interplay of computer science and pure mathematics (theoretical CS).

entry.title: Begin LaTeX in Minutes
entry.summary: A brief intro to LaTeX for beginners, in minutes.

entry.title: DBLP
entry.summary: The open bibliography database of computer science publications, with tidy author pages and conference volumes. Against Google Scholar it is clean and hand-maintained — author ambiguity and phantom records are rare.

entry.title: Computer History Museum
entry.summary: Oral history interviews with the pioneers of computing, plus a lecture archive. Unlike technical channels it records the circumstances a decision was made in — the context no document holds.

entry.title: Nature
entry.summary: One of science’s most prestigious peer-reviewed journals, carrying news and research together. Unlike preprint archives its strict peer review gives published findings their weight.

entry.title: OpenStax
entry.summary: A Rice University project offering university textbooks free and openly licensed. Unlike commercial texts it gives full, peer-reviewed volumes that are free and regularly updated.

entry.title: PhET Simulations
entry.summary: The University of Colorado’s interactive simulations for physics, chemistry and maths. Unlike a lecture it lets you experience a concept by tweaking its parameters by hand.

entry.title: Semantic Scholar
entry.summary: An AI-powered academic search engine. Unlike Google Scholar it summarises a paper, distinguishes influential citations and extracts links semantically.

entry.title: Connected Papers
entry.summary: A tool that starts from one paper and builds a visual graph of related work. Unlike a citation list it draws a “map” of a field and shows neighbouring work.

entry.title: SKYbrary
entry.summary: An aviation safety knowledge base of accident analyses, human factors and safety management systems — a usable archive for anyone thinking about high-reliability system design.

entry.title: İÜ Gazete Arşivi
entry.summary: Istanbul University’s scanned historical newspaper collection — primary sources for period research, where the details secondary literature skips turn up.

entry.title: Nişanyan Yeradları
entry.summary: A historical inventory of settlement names in and around Turkey, documenting each change with date and source. Nothing else compiles this systematically.

entry.title: David Rumsey Harita Koleksiyonu
entry.summary: A high-resolution historical map archive that lets you georeference maps onto modern geography — a strong tool for tracking place-name and border change.

entry.title: Transkribus · Osmanlıca
entry.summary: A text-recognition model trained on printed Ottoman Turkish. General OCR cannot read Arabic-script Turkish, and that gap is critical in archive research.

entry.title: ABD Antarktika Programı
entry.summary: The official portal of the Antarctic research programme, with material on field logistics and station operations — an interesting source on systems that work in extreme conditions.

entry.title: Devlet Arşivleri
entry.summary: Turkey’s official archive institution and the gateway to catalogues and digital copies of Ottoman and Republican-era documents.

entry.title: Aperta
entry.summary: TÜBİTAK’s open archive, hosting research data alongside publications. Data sharing is not yet common in Turkey, which makes it notable.

entry.title: Harman
entry.summary: A harvester searching Turkey’s institutional academic archives from one place, replacing the university-by-university hunt for theses and articles.

entry.title: DergiPark
entry.summary: The open-access platform for Turkish academic journals, hosting over a thousand titles — the primary source for Turkish literature, not aggregated anywhere else.

entry.title: Wolfram Alpha
entry.summary: A computational knowledge engine that integrates, converts units and compares data. A search engine finds the answer; this computes it, showing the working step by step in the paid tier.

entry.title: iNaturalist
entry.summary: Share nature observations and get species identified; once the community confirms one, the record becomes research-grade and flows into GBIF. A rare case of a hobby producing real data.

entry.title: Ethnologue
entry.summary: The standard catalogue of world languages with systematic speaker counts and vitality ratings. It is also the registration authority for ISO 639-3 language codes.

entry.title: Open Language Archives Community
entry.summary: A community uniting language resource archives under a shared metadata standard — the infrastructure that makes scattered university collections searchable.

entry.title: Open Language Archives (arama)
entry.summary: Searches language resources across scattered institutional archives from one place, particularly useful for material on under-documented and endangered languages.

entry.title: Vikipedi Portalları
entry.summary: An index of Wikipedia’s topic portals — a structured way into a field instead of random search, and a way not to enter a new subject without a map.

entry.title: Arkhe Projesi
entry.summary: Turkish science and philosophy writing that sits between the shallowness of popular science and the opacity of academic register.

entry.title: SkyViewer
entry.summary: Browses sky survey data by position, letting you overlay telescope imagery and compare across wavelengths.

entry.title: Oxford Academic
entry.summary: Oxford University Press’s journal platform, one of the major publisher archives. Most content sits behind subscription, with open-access articles separately marked.
